title: Republicans got Trumped. So now what?
content:
The midterms exposed deep frustration with war, fuel costs and executive overreach – leaving the party’s post-election path uncertain

On the same day that he led his Republican Party into a midterm electoral slaughter, US President Donald Trump told Fox News that he would move to Israel to “become Prime Minister” if Americans “got tired” of him.

This sounds like one of those “I’m moving to Canada if I lose” things. Except that he can’t actually threaten to move to Canada. Because even some of the most populist right-wing Canadians hate him for being unable to shut up about annexing their country.

He and his apparently unquenchable thirst for colonization could head over to Israel and spend his retirement fighting with Iran from right next door. It would last about 20 minutes when Democrats cut all funding and support. Think their voters are upset about paying for Bibi’s wars? Imagine how tight-fisted they’d be with ‘Trump’s Israel.’ Iran wins, opens the Strait of Hormuz, global fuel prices stabilize, and Trump finally gets a Nobel Peace Prize for single-handedly regime changing two of the biggest global pariahs.

Barely a few hours after the midterms, Trump was already warming up to the idea of just vetoing anything that the Democrat-majority Congress tries to do. Sources close to him say that he’d also resort to executive orders. All of which would leave Congress to prioritize spending their time impeaching him and hauling his enablers and sycophants in front of congressional hearings. Great plan!

Trump doesn’t much see himself as the problem in this election, suggesting that it was the GOP candidates who weren’t up to par. Of course they weren’t – they had to be tailored to his personal satisfaction to even survive the primary process, thoroughly disqualifying them in the eyes of everyone else.

Read more

He did recognize that Americans don’t like high fuel prices, but nonetheless considers that they just need to deal with it as he suicide bombs the American economy to assuage Bibi’s perpetual fever dream of Iran getting nukes. But more probably because his family and cronies are wheeling and dealing with Israel and the checks won’t clear until the dirty work is done. 

But here’s what we know about how Americans really feel from exit polling that surveyed about the same percentage of Republicans and Democrats. Most of them (60%) considered their Congressional vote little more than a Trump performance review. Most of them (53%) strongly disapprove of the job that he’s doing. Only 37% believe that he’s been fighting for people like them – the average American – with 62% feeling that he prioritizes his own personal interests over the nation’s, and made the economy worse (65%). They don’t even particularly like the Democrats (35% “strongly unfavorably”), and admit to being hardcore capitalists (57%), but they still think that the Democrats would do a better economic job than Trump at this point.

Americans across party lines feel overwhelmingly (71%) that the Republican-majority Congress abdicated its constitutional duty to exercise checks and balances on Trump’s executive powers.

The top voting issue was the domestic economy (39%) with cost of living a major consideration for 89% of voters. Their last priority was foreign policy at just 4%. In other words, by starting an economy-crushing war with Iran for his Israeli donors, Trump was literally doing the polar opposite of what Americans wanted him to focus on.

Read more

Three quarters of voters even cited the Iran war as a major factor in their electoral choice. But Trump wouldn’t know that from watching Fox News’ neocon slop all day long. Or from consulting with the ego fluffers who surround him and obviously only tell him what they think he wants to hear. Or from obsessively scrolling in the algorithmically-controlled echo chambers rife with nutjob influencers and bots, curated by the tech broligarchy more interested in government contracts and influence than the priorities of the average American.

At least in Israel, his policy passions actually might have a shot at aligning with those of the electorate. Because in the US, where a whopping 3% of the voters are Jewish, two-thirds of them still voted Democrat.

So what’s next for right-wing populism in America? For now, it’s homeless. No one within a mile of Trump has any appeal.

title: Israel’s president gives Eisenkot the first chance to form the next government
content:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog formally gave opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form the next government Sunday evening.

Complex coalition negotiations still lie ahead, but it marked a significant step in the former military chief's effort to oust Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, after elections held in a deeply divided country. Israel remains scarred by the Hamas-led attacks of Oct. 7, 2023, and the multifront wars they triggered.

I hope with all my heart that whatever government is formed will lead to unity, connection and healing among all segments of our people for our very existence depends on it, and we have only one country, Herzog said at the ceremony at the presidential residence in Jerusalem.

The announcement doesn't guarantee that Eisenkot, a former army chief, will become the next prime minister. He has up to six weeks to form a coalition government by securing alliances, a daunting challenge because the Oct. 27 election gave neither his bloc nor Netanyahus a clear majority in parliament.

Herzog said that in consultations with the parties, a majority of members of parliament, known as the Knesset, supported giving Eisenkot this task.

At Sunday's ceremony, Eisenkot promised to give the country leadership that people can trust, that will act in the interests of the public and that represents all parts of society.

An absolute majority of Knesset members representing the Israeli public support change, he said. I intend to navigate the situation with patience, humility, composure and a deep commitment to a Jewish, equal, liberal, and secure Israel.

Politically fraught coalition choices lie ahead

Among the possible kingmakers and most politically fraught potential allies are the Arab-led parties. They made historic gains in the election thanks to high voter turnout among Israel's Arab citizens.

Only one Arab party, Raam, has ever joined a governing coalition, in 2021. Raam has said it will support Eisenkot, but the party does not have enough seats on its own to give Eisenkot a parliamentary majority.

Breaking with decades of precedent, the second Arab-led party, the Joint List, has offered to support Eisenkot from outside the coalition to end Netanyahus grip on power.

But that cooperation is fraught for both sides. For the Joint List, it would mean backing a government unlikely to end Israels wars or curb settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank. For Eisenkot and other opposition parties, it would mean aligning with parties that not only criticize Israels policies but reject its identity as a Jewish state.

One of Eisenkots partners, the more conservative Yisrael Beytenu party, already has said it will not join a coalition with Arab-led parties.

Eisenkot has laid out four conditions for parties that want to join him. They must recognize Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, accept its declaration of independence, support military, national or civil service for all citizens, and declare the Hamas militant group a terrorist group. It remains unclear whether his would-be Arab partners are ready to accept these conditions.

Furthermore, Netanyahu has repeatedly asserted unsubstantiated claims that the election was stolen by Arab parties. In a pressure tactic on Eisenkot, he says any alliance with these parties would be an act of betrayal.

Israels Shin Bet security agency has launched an investigation into possible foreign interference in the vote, but the countrys Central Elections Committee and Herzog say the vote was valid and even if wrongdoing is found, it did not have a significant impact on the electoral results.

Eisenkot faces significant challenges on the road to becoming prime minister

Eisenkot has vowed to form a government as quickly as possible. But each likely scenario appears to entail compromises or broken promises.

Aside from seeking the support of the Arab-led parties, Eisenkot has two options: a power-sharing agreement with Netanyahu or an agreement with the ultra-Orthodox parties, which demand military exemptions for their community.

Eisenkot and his partners made equal military service a central part of their campaign. Specifically, they are seeking an end to the long-standing draft exemptions.

The religious parties, which were part of Netanyahus outgoing coalition, want to preserve them, calling them essential to their devout lifestyle. But the exemptions have grown especially controversial among the broader public during the past three years of war.

Anticipating its position as a swing vote, the ultra-Orthodox party United Torah Judaism has left the door open to cooperating with Eisenkot.

Eisenkot has 28 days to form a coalition, with a possible two-week extension from the president. If he is unable to form a government, Netanyahu could then be given a chance to put together a coalition. If Netanyahu is also unable to do so, the country would return to elections early next spring.

Israels new members of Knesset will be sworn in on Tuesday evening. Netanyahu and his cabinet will remain in office in a caretaker capacity, with limited powers, until a coalition is formed.

Wars, international support remain big challenges for next government

Despite tenuous ceasefires, Israel's military remains engaged in fighting Hamas militants in Gaza and Iran-backed Hezbollah militants in Lebanon and the war the country launched jointly with the United States against Iran remains unresolved as well.

Both Eisenkot and Herzog mentioned these challenges on Sunday, as well as what Herzog called the new political situation in the United States," where the midterm elections suggested weakening support for Israel on both sides of the aisle.

He called on Eisenkot to use his military leadership skills as well as his experience of loss, since Eisenkot lost a son in combat in Gaza to unite the country.

You have commanded soldiers from every part of the Israeli people and Israeli society. Your face bears the scars of bullets from decades of command and combat, Herzog said. In the coming days, Gadi, as you and your counterparts enter the negotiating rooms, I ask that you remember that the eyes of the entire nation, with all its pain, hopes, prayers, and fears, are upon you.

title: Seven dead as trains collide in Egypt (VIDEOS)
content:
The rear-end crash south of Cairo left 110 injured and several train carriages derailed

Seven people have been killed and 110 injured in a violent train collision in Egypt that hurled several passenger carriages off the tracks.

The crash occurred on Sunday in the Al-Ayyat district of Giza province, south of Cairo, when one passenger train slammed into the rear of another, according to Egyptian Railways.

Footage from the scene shows derailed train cars and twisted wreckage as rescuers and locals scramble to help passengers trapped inside. Emergency crews also brought in cranes to clear the tracks.

President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi ordered an urgent investigation into the collision and pledged to hold anyone found responsible for negligence accountable. The cause of the crash has not yet been established.

Egypt has suffered repeated deadly railway accidents despite billions of dollars invested in modernizing its network. Poor maintenance, aging infrastructure, and management failures have long plagued the system. Two major crashes just weeks apart in 2021 killed 30 people and injured nearly 300.

READ MORE: Dozens killed in Spanish high-speed train collision (VIDEOS)

The Al-Ayyat district was also the scene of Egypt’s deadliest railway disaster in 2002, when a fire swept through an overcrowded passenger train, killing more than 370 people.

title: Ukrainians in Germany in no rush to return home – media
content:
A Berlin counseling center has received just 60 inquiries about returning since April

The vast majority of Ukrainian migrants residing in Germany are not considering returning home in the foreseeable future, Rheinische Post has reported, citing figures attributed to the Unity Hub Berlin counseling center.

Since the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in 2022, Germany has become the top destination for Ukrainian migrants within the European Union, taking in nearly 1.3 million people, according to Eurostat. Earlier this year, the German Press Agency (dpa), citing the German Interior Ministry’s figures, reported that as of the end of May, 265,804 Ukrainian men of fighting age were living in Germany.

Even though the Ukrainian authorities imposed a general mobilization shortly after the escalation of the conflict with Russia, barring most able-bodied men ageds 22 to 60 from leaving the country, many have still managed to cross the border illegally and reached the EU.

In its article on Tuesday, Rheinische Post cited data from Unity Hub Berlin. Since the counseling center opened in April, it has received only around “60 inquiries regarding the possibilities of returning to Ukraine,” according to the publication. Just three of those reportedly came from men of military age.

“The overwhelming majority of those making inquiries are only considering a return once active hostilities have definitively ceased and the security situation in Ukraine has stabilized,” the newspaper reported, citing the counseling center’s data.

According to Rheinische Post, as of late October, Unity Hub Berlin “had no confirmed statistical data” on how many Ukrainian migrants had moved beyond initial inquiries and actually begun preparing to return home.

In recent months, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s coalition government has progressively ramped up pressure on Ukrainian migrants.

Read more

In June, Markus Soeder, the leader of Bavaria’s Christian Social Union (CSU) – the sister party of Merz’s Christian Democratic Party (CDU) – called for unemployed Ukrainian migrants to be stripped of access to Germany’s unemployment and welfare benefits system, including Buergergeld (citizens’ benefits) payments.

Soeder, who serves as governor of Bavaria, also urged the authorities in Berlin “to increase deportations and voluntary departures to drastically reduce costs.”

Meanwhile, as Ukrainian forces suffer mounting losses and the pool of willing recruits continues to shrink, draft enforcement squads have increasingly turned to violent methods to fill the ranks in recent months. Men are being snatched from streets, workplaces, and residential areas, as evidenced by hundreds of videos circulating online.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt also announced in July that his country would stop granting automatic temporary protection to Ukrainians fleeing conscription.

Following a meeting with Ukrainian leader Vladimir Zelensky in April, Chancellor Merz stated that Berlin and Kiev would also coordinate efforts to return military-age Ukrainian men residing in Germany to their home country.

Zelensky welcomed Berlin’s approach, saying that “of course, our armed forces would want these people to return to Ukraine.”

Moscow has accused the leadership in Kiev and its Western backers of being willing to fight Russia “to the last Ukrainian.”

title: Israel issues new threat to Iran
content:
The Jewish state’s defense minister has accused Tehran of reviving its nuclear weapons ambitions and warned of further military action

Israel is not done with Iran, Defense Minister Israel Katz has warned. He accused Tehran of reviving its nuclear weapons ambitions and vowed to pursue offensive military action to counter any threats.

The threat follows new US strikes against Iranian air defenses and reports that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has pressed Washington to launch another major offensive.

“With regard to Iran, the mission is still not complete. Iran is trying to renew its efforts to obtain nuclear weapons,” Katz said on Sunday, as cited by Israeli media.

Tehran has consistently denied seeking nuclear weapons and maintains that its nuclear program serves peaceful purposes.

Read more

US President Donald Trump claimed in late October that US-Israeli strikes had destroyed Iran’s nuclear enrichment capabilities but acknowledged that some suspect sites remained. The IAEA has found no evidence that Tehran has rebuilt damaged facilities, although it remains unable to verify Iran’s enriched uranium stockpiles.

On Friday, Trump confirmed “minor strikes” against Iranian air defenses on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, but insisted Washington had made “a lot of progress” in negotiations with Tehran.

The US and Israel launched a major offensive against Iran on February 28 with the stated goals of destroying its nuclear and missile capabilities and bringing about regime change. Despite the killing of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and other senior officials, Iran’s government remains in power.

On Saturday, Iran’s military declared itself stronger than at the start of the war, while the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had lifted its self-imposed 2,000 km limit on missile range. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned last week that renewed US-Israeli attacks would trigger an immediate response without geographical restrictions.

READ MORE: Israeli president instructs Netanyahu rival to form government

Netanyahu’s coalition lost Israel’s October 27 election, while Trump’s Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s US midterms, partly due to public frustration over the Iran war.

Reuters reported on Thursday that Tehran had submitted a proposal to Washington through Qatar, which the US was reviewing. Iran has demanded an end to US sanctions and its naval blockade as conditions for resuming negotiations.

READ MORE: Iran won’t surrender. Can Russia give Trump another way out?

Russia has backed a diplomatic settlement. President Vladimir Putin met Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei on Thursday to discuss the conflict and regional security.

title: Democrats plotting to undermine Trump on Ukraine – FT
content:
The party is planning to spend more US taxpayer money propping up Kiev and tightening sanctions against Russia, the paper reports

The US Democratic Party is preparing a new $15 billion package for Ukraine alongside tougher sanctions against Russia, the Financial Times reported on Saturday. The party is reportedly seeking to undermine progress made on resolving the Ukraine conflict made by US President Donald Trump, following its victory in midterm elections.

The Democrats are seeking to revive Biden-era policies even before the new Congress convenes in January, with energy assistance being “really, really high on our list,” an unnamed aide told the newspaper.

The party could reportedly seek to attach Ukraine-related provisions, including support for its energy infrastructure and air defenses, to the annual National Defense Authorization Act. However, any new legislation will be complicated by the Republicans retaining control of both chambers until January, and Trump’s potential veto of new bills afterwards.

Read more

According to the paper, another major priority is tightening sanctions against Moscow, particularly by amending legislation championed by the late Republican Senator and anti-Russian hawk Lindsey Graham.

Trump signed the bill in September but subsequently waived major provisions, arguing that enforcing them would interfere with efforts to negotiate a settlement. His administration also struck a deal with Moscow in early October allowing Russian diesel to return to American and international markets.

Read more

Democrats are additionally considering putting pressure on key Trump officials, including investigations into the business interests of presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, both of whom spearheaded Ukraine conflict mediation efforts and diplomatic overtures to Moscow, according to the FT. They also reportedly want greater scrutiny of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite network, which Ukrainian forces rely on for communications.

Read more

Washington has already poured enormous resources into Ukraine under former US President Joe Biden. Since 2022, Congress has appropriated more than $196 billion related to the conflict, including military aid, US stockpile replenishment, and economic support. Some previously authorized deliveries have continued during Trump’s second term.

Although American support for Kiev initially enjoyed broad bipartisan backing, a growing number of Republicans subsequently opposed what they called Biden’s “blank-check” policies.

Trump himself has blasted Biden over what he called excessive spending on Ukraine and has resisted approving new US-funded aid packages. His administration has instead focused on selling American weapons to European NATO members, who then transferred them to Kiev.

The Trump administration has suspended some assistance on a couple of occasions, including in the aftermath of his heated row with Ukrainian leader Vladimir Zelensky in the Oval Office in February 2025.

Zelensky, meanwhile, claimed on Thursday that the US had failed to deliver $16 billion in previously promised assistance to Kiev, insisting that Ukraine “must fight” to secure the outstanding funds.

Moscow has repeatedly denounced Western arms shipments to Kiev, arguing they only prolong the conflict without changing its outcome.

title: EU-wide data center protests take aim at Brussels (VIDEOS)
content:
Thousands have hit the streets across the bloc to demand a halt to energy-hungry AI infrastructure projects

A wave of protests against energy-guzzling and water-intensive AI data centers has swept across the EU, with thousands demanding a halt to new projects over their environmental impact.

Brussels is pushing to at least triple the bloc’s data center capacity within five to seven years. First announced in April 2025, the target was reinforced this June with proposed legislation to fast-track construction by easing permits and access to land, energy, and water.

The two-day campaign, organized by the Stop Dirty Data Centres coalition, brought together more than 100 groups demanding a moratorium on large-scale projects. Activists warn that the facilities could compete with homes and businesses for electricity and water, drive up energy bills, and strain infrastructure. They also cite AI-related risks, including job losses, mass surveillance, and mental health problems.

In France, protesters marched through the northern Pas-de-Calais Department on Saturday to oppose a massive data center planned near Corbehem and Brebieres. Similar demonstrations were planned in Paris and the Marseille area.

In Finland, around 1,300 people marched through Helsinki according to police, passing Google’s offices before gathering outside parliament. Protests also took place in five other cities over electricity consumption, deforestation and weak regulation.

THE CLOUD IS NOT ABOVE THE LAW: WHO OWNS OUR WATER, LAND AND FUTURE? When Big Tech builds its AI empire, who pays the environmental price? SOURCE CREDIT Campaign: [Stop Dirty Data Centres – European Days of Action, 6–7 November 2026](https://t.co/ndcxPEJAsX). WHAT IS HAPPENING IN FINLAND? On 7 November, people marched in Helsinki from Railway Square, past Google's office, towards Parliament, demanding a moratorium on new data-centre projects. More than 100 organisations across 15 European countries joined the wider campaign. This protest follows serious environmental concerns surrounding Google's proposed data centres in Muhos and Kajaani. Finnish authorities ordered construction-related preparatory work suspended pending environmental impact assessments. Police have also opened a preliminary investigation into suspected environmental damage at the Muhos site. Euronews +2 THE ENVIRONMENTAL COST OF AI Data centres are not virtual infrastructure. They occupy land, consume electricity, require cooling water and generate heat. The expansion of artificial intelligence is creating enormous demand for physical resources. Communities should not be expected to sacrifice forests, groundwater, biodiversity and affordable electricity for corporate expansion. WHY INDIA MUST PAY ATTENTION India is already facing this challenge. According to WRI India, more than half of the country's data centres are located in water-stressed regions. A February 2026 CEEW study estimates that Indian data centres consumed approximately 150 billion litres of water annually, with consumption expected to more than double by 2030. Yet sustainability provisions are explicitly included in only five of the 15 state policies examined in that study. WRI India +1 These figures demand public scrutiny, transparent reporting and enforceable environmental safeguards. THE DEMOCRATIC QUESTION Technological progress cannot become an excuse for corporate impunity. Governments must not allow powerful technology companies to dictate how public resources are allocated without meaningful consultation with affected communities. People deserve to know how much water and electricity these facilities consume, where the resources come from, what environmental damage they cause and who bears the cost. WHAT MUST CHANGE? * Independent environmental and water-impact assessments before approvals. * Public disclosure of water and electricity consumption. * Protection of forests, groundwater and biodiversity. * Mandatory renewable-energy and water-recycling standards. * Independent monitoring and meaningful penalties for violations. * A moratorium on large projects until enforceable safeguards are established. THE FINAL WORD AI must serve humanity, not turn nature into a corporate resource. The question is not whether society should embrace technology. It is whether technological progress should be allowed to undermine ecological survival, public welfare and democratic accountability. Finland's protesters have sent an important message. India must listen before its own communities are left paying the price. Water belongs to people, not corporations. The planet is not Big Tech's private resource. Further reading and reporting * [Yle: Police investigate Google's Muhos data-centre activities](https://t.co/PEuyIEmjf5). * [Euronews: Finland suspends Google's data-centre projects](https://t.co/dYAS3wtVyV). * [Euronews: European protests against energy-hungry data centres](https://t.co/qIMjZVqStj). * [CEEW: India's data-centre infrastructure, power and water use](https://t.co/LidkOZm05k). * [WRI India: Data centres and water stress](https://t.co/KMFkBHdD5c). *

— Ashok Dadhwal (@ashokdadhwal196) November 8, 2026

In Berlin, activists rallied outside data centers on Friday with banners reading ‘Data centers? No thank you!’ Environmental groups also held a conference the next day to discuss resistance to new projects.

In Amsterdam, hundreds stormed a Microsoft data center construction site on Friday, cutting through fences, climbing cranes and clashing with riot police. Police detained 218 people, who were all released the following day, Dutch media reported. One officer sustained minor injuries, while the authorities reported property damage and suspected theft.

The campaign also reached the UK, with actions organized in London, Reading, and Northern Ireland. Another protest is planned in Edinburgh on November 14.

The demonstrations were planned weeks earlier but gained momentum after the US midterms, according to industry publication DatacenterDynamics. Candidates opposing data center expansion scored victories, while voters in several areas approved construction restrictions.

Ahead of the protests, EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen defended building more facilities but told Reuters that they must not drive up electricity bills, cause blackouts, or harm the environment.

title: Gunman who killed at least 6 in Kraków mass shooting has died in hospital
content:
A gunman who killed at least six people during a deadly rampage in the Polish city of Krakw on Saturday has died in hospital, Reuters news agency reported on Monday, citing police.

The country was horrified by the rare mass shooting in the historic main square of the city in the countrys south, which prompted national mourning and heightened security, as authorities said the attack was likely driven by far-right ideology.

The Polish citizen, in his 20s, was shot and injured by police during the attack before being transported to hospital. There, he underwent multiple surgeries and had been in a critical condition prior to his death.

The mass shooting which authorities said they are investigating as a possible terror attack has generated a wave of fear in a European nation with exceptionally tight gun laws.

Krakw police said the gunman drove into the citys main market square, typically popular with tourists and locals, and started firing randomly at people, initially from his car, killing four women and two men, on Saturday afternoon. Sixteen others were injured, including two police officers.

The alleged attacker was wearing military-style clothing and used military weapons, Police Deputy Inspector Katarzyna Ciso told Polish news outlet TVN24. Weapons and ammunition were also found in his vehicle.

The bodies of his sister, mother and father were later found at the suspects home in the town of Ostrowiec witokrzyski, about 120 miles northeast of Krakw. Polands prosecutors office said Sunday that it is highly likely the killings were carried out by the same person, but investigations were ongoing.

Eleven firearms were recovered from both sites, the prosecutors office spokesperson said.

Gunmans clothing examined

Little is known about the gunman, who has not been identified by police, and his motive was not immediately clear. But Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiski said that the shooter was fascinated with far-right ideologies and held very radical views.

Emblems on his clothing were being examined by experts, an interior ministry spokesperson said on Monday.

These patches were associated with various motifs that are currently being analyzed by specialists, Karolina Galecka told radio TOK FM, Reuters reported.

The suspect was a member of a shooting club and appeared to be highly skilled marksman, the club spokesperson Adam Chyb told Reuters on Sunday.

Poland, like other European Union countries, has strict rules about acquiring guns and very few people are allowed to own military-style weapons or carry guns in public. About 411,000 people have gun permits in the country, which has a population of more than 37 million, according to the Associated Press.

Off-duty surgeons saved lives

An off-duty surgeon who rushed to the scene of the shooting to treat victims of the attack, including a police officer, said he had just finished eating lunch with his family when he heard what sounded like gunshots.

Michal Pedziwiatr described being in the eye of the storm as he and a friend also a surgeon began providing care to the wounded.

Pedziwiatr told a press conference on Sunday that his friend, Mateusz Wierdak, was a hero for saving the life of a police officer who subdued the attacker, after he applied pressure to the bleeding wound without any protective gear or gloves and stuffed gauze pads into the chest cavity, Reuters reported.

The two wounded police officers, who Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk praised for also saving many lives, underwent surgery and remain in hospital, police said.

title: Pope wraps up Uruguay visit and heads to most fraught stop of his tour in Milei's Argentina
content:
Pope Leo XIV wrapped up his visit to Uruguay on Sunday by marking an important Catholic feast day that is tied to the countrys independence, capping his effort to draw attention to the role the church played in the founding of Latin Americas most secular country.

Leo traveled to the city of Florida, north of Montevideo, before heading to Argentina for the second leg of his three-nation tour of South America. It's expected to be the most politically delicate, given the Catholic Church's sharp criticisms of the austerity program of libertarian President Javier Milei.

For his final event in Uruguay, Leo was commemorating the feast of the Virgin of the Thirty-three. Every year, thousands of pilgrims flock to Florida on the second Sunday of every November to pray before the small wooden icon of the Virgin Mary housed there.

IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Pope Leo XIV casts mail-in ballot, becoming first pope to vote in US election

According to tradition, 33 independence patriots acquired the Guaran statue and had it with them when independence was declared from the Brazilian empire in Florida on Aug. 25, 1825.

Leo became the first pope in nearly four decades to visit Uruguay, in hopes of reminding its people that the Catholic Church is part of their very identity as a nation even if in subsequent decades the country went on a deeply secular, and at times anticlerical, route.

Thousands of people poured into Florida's main square on Sunday ahead of the Mass under brilliant blue skies, some walking for several kilometers (miles) to reach the site.

An assessment after the first leg of the trip

Leo was hoping to leave a parting message before opening the second leg of his South American trip, which he went ahead with despite having undergone surgery Oct. 13 to remove a cancerous tumor from his lung. The final stop is in Peru, his second homeland.

Leo, 71, has appeared in fine form at his events, singing loudly, bounding up stairs and gamely greeting the crowds in his popemobile. He has not cut any events short, including those that have kept him out until past midnight Rome time.

This visit will also serve to reinforce the image of Leo as a leader, not merely in a spiritual sense, but in a much broader capacity as a political leader and a widely recognized figure who, far from shying away from conflict or tension, offers a powerful perspective and commands a highly respected voice, said Luis Bahamondes, a professor at the Center for Judaic Studies at the University of Chile.

A potentially delicate meeting with Milei

In Buenos Aires, Milei is due to greet Leo at the airport and then the two will appear together for the traditional welcome ceremony and exchange of speeches. The encounter could be tense, given the Catholic Church's criticism of Mileis austerity measures that have slashed social spending, and his embrace of artificial intelligence.

Milei has staked his presidency on cutting social spending to overhaul Argentinas troubled economy and deliver a long-elusive budget surplus. He has called social justice an aberration that amounts to stealing, and mocked as huge stupidity the increasingly common complaint in Argentina that families squeezed by his austerity program cant make it to the end of the month.

Leo, who took his name from the 19th-century pope whose encyclical on labor laid the foundation of Catholic social teaching, has made the poor and vulnerable a focus of his papacy, carrying on the legacy of his Argentine predecessor, Pope Francis.

Posters reading At last, a Lion who unites appeared across Buenos Aires this weekend, a jab playing on the popes name in Spanish Len, or lion and the lion imagery Milei often uses to portray himself on social media.

Argentina is a society currently experiencing significant upheaval, deep polarization, and an economic crisis, along with a president who defies conventional protocol a leader who, at one point, even challenged Pope Francis, Bahamondes said.

The Argentine church is a sharp Milei critic

Since taking office in December 2023, Milei has slashed Argentinas health care budget by 48% in real terms. Planned cuts to the public university system, which represents a near-universal point of pride in the crisis-prone country, sent students into the streets.

According to official data, poverty in Argentina reached 32.3% of the population during the first half of 2026, representing about 15 million people.

Much like its allies in the Trump administration, Milei's government has portrayed the cuts as part of a necessary reform process to remake Argentinas troubled economy and eliminate fraud and waste in the federal bureaucracy.

Like Trump, Milei has also courted AI investment and data centers with promises of limited regulation. Leo has warned that the AI race poses threats to humanity and the environment and called for strict, internationally policed safeguards on its development.

Mileis government insists the papal trip is purely religious. The pope belongs to all Argentines. He doesnt belong to a political party or a political camp, Karina Milei, the presidents sister and secretary general of the presidency, told reporters after a recent planning meeting for Leos visit with church leaders.

A trip to complete Francis unfinished business

In Argentina, Leo is completing unfinished business left by his predecessor, Francis. The Argentine Jesuit, the former archbishop of Buenos Aires, never returned home during his 12-year pontificate, confounding friends and foes alike.

Theres a lot of disagreement over Francis and his legacy in Argentina, said David Lantigua, a theology professor and faculty fellow at the University of Notre Dames Kellogg Institute, which focuses especially on Latin American affairs.

Much of the polemics stems from his tenure in Buenos Aires, when the former Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio was a sometimes divisive partisan figure in a politically polarized country. Bergoglio was a slum priest, who advocated for the poorest and most marginalized the sector of Argentines feeling Mileis social spending cuts the most.

I think well see that kind of tension with Leo thats the ministry Francis left behind, Lantigua said.

Leo, who spent two decades as a missionary priest in Peru ministering to poor people, is very much a pastor in Francis' image and owes his pontificate to the late pope.

Argentinas state intelligence agency said Saturday that a person had been arrested over death threats against Leo ahead of his visit to the country. A federal court in Campana, some 70 kilometers (45 miles) northwest of Buenos Aires, ordered the arrest less than 24 hours after the agency was tipped off, it said, without elaborating on the suspect or the nature of the threat.

title: Chinese space station to welcome first foreign astronaut
content:
A Pakistani national will orbit the Earth as part of the Shenzhou-24 mission, Beijing has said

A Pakistani national will become the first foreign astronaut to visit China’s Tiangong space station, Beijing has said.

He will join the crew of the Shenzhou-24 mission, which blasts off for the station on November 25, as a payload specialist, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) announced on Saturday.

The Pakistani astronaut’s stay in orbit will be a rather short one, as he is scheduled to return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft, it said. The mission is expected to conclude on November 30.

Two Pakistani representatives – Khurram Daud and Muhammad Zeeshan Ali – were selected to undergo training in China after a three-stage selection and assessment process. CMSA did not say which would travel to Tiangong and who will serve as a backup.

So far, only Chinese taikonauts have worked at the station, which began operating in low orbit in 2021.

Read more

After Beijing and Islamabad signed a cooperation agreement on a manned space flight in February 2025, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif hailed the development as “a defining moment in the nation’s space journey, emphasizing that it will be remembered as a cornerstone of Pakistan’s aspiration in human spaceflight.”

CMSA chief Lin Xiqiang said that “Pakistan’s participation in the China Space Station program reflects the deep-rooted ties between the two countries and will contribute to mutual knowledge-sharing and the broader vision of peaceful space exploration for the benefit of humanity.”

Shenzhou-24 will mark only the second-ever Pakistani national going to space. The pioneer was Namira Salim, who experienced several minutes of weightlessness as part of a “suborbital” flight with the Virgin Galactic space tourism company in 2023.

Last week, China laid out a roadmap for a manned lunar program consisting of four missions and culminating in a crewed touchdown on the Moon “before 2030.”

Several years ago, Moscow and Beijing announced a joint International Lunar Research Station (ILRS) project, with Russia seeking to build a power station on Earth’s only natural satellite to provide energy for a base within the next decade.

READ MORE: Japan launches historic mission for Mars moon samples

In April, the head of the Russian space agency, Roscosmos, Dmitry Bakanov, said that the country’s Academy of Sciences had approved the concept for establishing the Russian segment of the lunar base. At the same time, Moscow is developing its own tools to scan the Moon and study its structure, he added.

title: US to target Iran’s land-based supply routes – CENTCOM
content:
The effort is set to reinforce Washington’s ongoing sea blockade of Tehran’s ports, Admiral Brad Cooper has said

The US military has announced the creation of a new task force which will be dedicated to disrupting land-based supply routes to Iran.

The Task Force Iron Gate is being set up to reinforce Washington’s ongoing sea blockade of the Islamic Republic’s ports, the commander of US Central Command (CENTCOM), Admiral Brad Cooper, said in a statement on Saturday.

Ending the naval blockade is among Tehran’s key demands for settling the conflict with the US and allowing the resumption of shipping via the Strait of Hormuz, which normally accounts for around 20% of global crude trade.

The task force, which will be based in Tampa, Florida and staffed with some 20 civilian and military personnel, will focus on “preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea.” It will operate in coordination with other US government agencies, CENTCOM said.

Read more

Reuters reported earlier that its investigation has established that Tehran had been successful in evading both the US naval blockade and the Western sanctions, importing at least $2 billion in hardware, explosives and heavy-duty trucks since the start of the year. According to the agency, the deliveries allegedly arrived by cargo ship across the Caspian Sea from Russia, by truck from Central ‌Asia, and by aircraft from China.

Moscow has previously denied claims that it is supplying weapons to the Islamic Republic, with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov saying that it’s “awkward to even hear about this.” The Iranian General Staff also stressed that “any commentary… on the purchase of equipment and weaponry from other countries lacks credibility.”

On Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Iranian Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei at the Kremlin. Bilateral cooperation and the security situation in the Middle East were discussed during the meeting, according to Moscow.

Read more

Rezaei’s visit to Russia came amid mounting concerns that large-scale hostilities between the US and Iran could resume following Tuesday’s US midterm election, in which the Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress from the Republicans. US Vice President J.D. Vance attributed his party’s crushing election defeat to the conflict with Tehran and the resulting spike in energy prices.

On Saturday, US President Donald Trump confirmed “minor strikes” against Iranian air defense systems on Qeshm Island in the Start of Hormuz, while also claiming that “a lot of progress” was made in Qatar-mediated talks between Washington and Tehran.

The same day, CENTCOM said that it had “disabled” a commercial vessel in the Gulf Of Oman that had “attempted to violate the naval blockade.”

CENTCOM forces disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman, Nov. 7, after the ship’s civilian crew ignored repeated warnings and attempted to violate the naval blockade against Iran multiple times. A U.S. military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of St. Kitts-flagged M/V Huda, disabling the ship after CENTCOM forces directed the crew to abandon targeted spaces. The cargo vessel tried to depart regional waters after visiting an Iranian port. Read the full release online: https://t.co/5wW1LqN1oW

— U.S. Central Command (@CENTCOM) November 7, 2026

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy reported that two oil tankers struck mines near the Strait of Hormuz after trying to traverse the waterway via an “unsafe” route, not designated by Tehran.

Rezaei issued a warning to the Trump administration on Saturday, writing on X that “you lost the war and the election. Vance has conceded... Start a war, and you’ll face a devastating response.”

title: Riot police unleash tear gas on French protesters (VIDEOS)
content:
Hundreds have been arrested as violent clashes spread across the country, with an RT correspondent caught in the chaos in Paris

French riot police have clashed with protesters across the country, firing tear gas and charging crowds as another wave of anti-government demonstrations swept through major cities on Saturday.

RT correspondent Yasin Eken witnessed the confrontation unfold in Paris’s Place de la Nation, reporting live as riot police moved in to disperse protesters.

“Up until this point, the protests have been largely peaceful, largely quiet,” Eken reported, describing how tensions escalated after several small fires broke out and police intervened. “Ever since then, it’s just been a constant back and forth between protesters and police.”

The square soon descended into chaos, with officers deploying tear gas and what Eken described as acoustic weapons, while demonstrators hurled rocks, bottles and other projectiles. As police reinforcements advanced from different sides of the square, Eken was forced to put on his gas mask and retreat.

— INFOS RÉVOLUTION (@Jujuukfj) November 7, 2026

Police claimed around 200 violent individuals attacked officers during the arrest of a man accused of setting fire to a rubbish bin. Some demonstrators reportedly threw projectiles and fireworks at security forces.

Saturday marked the fourth consecutive weekend of mass protests over living costs, wages and deteriorating conditions in schools. Organizers estimated nationwide turnout at 250,000, while the Interior Ministry counted 146,000, including 46,000 in Paris.

title: US offers millions for information on Iran’s nuclear program despite Trump’s claims of obliteration
content:
The United States is offering a reward of up to $20 million for information about Irans nuclear program, despite US President Donald Trumps repeated claims to have obliterated Tehrans capabilities.

Rewards for Justice (RFJ), a State Department program, is seeking tips on Irans nuclear facilities, equipment and associated personnel, the program said in a Friday social media post, which stated that relocation may be offered to informants.

During the 12-day conflict last year, Trump was quick to declare that Irans key nuclear enrichment facilities had been completely and totally obliterated. He kept up this assessment on several occasions after and attacked media organizations including CNN for challenging the claim.

Democratic leaders lay out plans for Congress after blue wave

This years conflict saw the US and Israel again attack Iranian nuclear sites, and Trump has made fresh claims to have tackled Irans threat, telling reporters on Friday that if we didnt hit Iran, you wouldnt have Israel today.

But the State Departments move and independent assessments suggest that concerns remain over Irans program, which Tehran has always insisted is peaceful.

Last year, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) reported that Iran was enriching uranium to 60% purity which is a short technical step from the 90% required for a nuclear weapon, according to an RFJ statement.

RELATED STORY | Vance blames Iran war for sweeping Republican midterm losses

Iran is the only non-nuclear-weapon state to produce uranium at such a high enrichment level. Experts estimate this quantity, if enriched further, could be enough for several nuclear weapons, it said.

It also referred to a loss of continuity of knowledge regarding Irans production and inventory of key components like centrifuges due to the regimes lack of compliance with the IAEA.

Preventing Iran from developing a nuclear weapon has been stated as a key objective for Washingtons war with Iran. This week, President Donald Trump repeated claims that the US might have to go after Irans Pickaxe Mountain, the suspected underground nuclear site where Israel believes Tehran has stored part of its enriched uranium stockpile and advanced enrichment centrifuges.

In response, Iran warned that any US attack on Iranian nuclear facilities would be treated as an expansion of the war in the region. Tehran maintains that it has the right to develop nuclear energy for peaceful purposes, including enrichment.

RFJ has also offered rewards for information on senior Iranian regime figures since the war began in February.

Mediators are continuing to try to broker an agreement between Iran and the US, but both sides appear unwilling to shift on key red lines, with Tehran seeing the ability to enrich uranium as a matter of national sovereignty.

Trump ordered new strikes on Iran overnight, describing them as minor.

Cost of war with Iran now at $47.1 billion

Explosions were heard on Irans Qeshm Island and in the southern Iranian port of Jask, Reuters reported on Saturday, citing Iranian media.

Iran has not officially confirmed the source of the reported explosions, according to Reuters.

Earlier on Saturday, Irans semi-official Tasnim news agency said two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, with no official information on potential damage. But later that evening Tasnim cited an Iranian source as saying that the explosions heard on the Island were not related to missile strikes.

In a separate development, CENTCOM has launched a task force with the intention of preventing Iran from accessing land routes that might facilitate the transportation of advanced weapons and other materials.

A naval blockade is already in place as part of US efforts to choke off Irans vital oil industry.

title: Israeli president instructs Netanyahu rival to form government
content:
Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot has secured the backing of 67 lawmakers, but faces a difficult task assembling a ruling coalition

Israeli President Isaac Herzog has announced that he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country’s next government, dealing a major political setback to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following last month’s inconclusive parliamentary elections.

Herzog informed both Eisenkot and Netanyahu of his decision on Saturday, and the former military chief, who heads the centrist Yashar party, will have 28 days to assemble a coalition, with a possible two-week extension.

During consultations earlier this week, Eisenkot secured the backing of 67 lawmakers in the 120-seat Knesset, compared to just 46 who recommended Netanyahu. However, the endorsements do not guarantee that he can assemble a functioning government.

Netanyahu’s Likud emerged as the largest single party in the October 27 election, but his right-wing and religious bloc secured only 53 seats, falling short of the 61 required for a parliamentary majority. Eisenkot’s four-party opposition alliance won just 48 seats, leaving the two Arab-led parties, which together control a record 19 seats, holding the balance of power.

Read more

Eisenkot has ruled out including the Arab parties in his government, while several of his allies have opposed even relying on their outside support. Another possibility involves an agreement with ultra-Orthodox parties traditionally allied with Netanyahu, although disagreements over exemptions from military service remain a major obstacle.

The ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party, which holds seven seats, notably declined to endorse Netanyahu during the presidential consultations and has signaled its openness to negotiations with Eisenkot.

Netanyahu, meanwhile, called on Saturday for a broad national unity government that would include his existing coalition partners, claiming that such an alliance would “permanently remove the nuclear threat from Iran.” He also warned that a government dependent on Arab parties, whom he accused of supporting Hamas, would threaten Israel’s survival.

Read more

Eisenkot’s Yashar party rejected the appeal, accusing Netanyahu of dividing Israeli society and inviting Likud to abandon its alliance with “extremists” and join a unity government under Eisenkot’s leadership.

The political deadlock follows a bitter election campaign overshadowed by the US-Israeli war on Iran, Israel’s military operations across the region, and divisions over Netanyahu’s leadership.

The incumbent campaigned on promises to resume the offensive against Tehran and overthrow its government, while Eisenkot questioned the need for another military campaign and accused Netanyahu of failing to achieve his previous war objectives.

Read more

Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, has held the office for more than 19 years across three separate stints. His repeated failures to assemble governing coalitions previously contributed to a prolonged political crisis that saw Israel hold five parliamentary elections between 2019 and 2022.

If Eisenkot fails to assemble a majority within the allotted period, Herzog could give another candidate, potentially Netanyahu, an opportunity to form a government. A prolonged stalemate could ultimately force Israel into another election.

title: Trump asks UFC boss to become White House press secretary
content:
The US president later said he “was kidding” about offering Dana White the job

US President Donald Trump offered UFC CEO Dana White the post of White House press secretary over the weekend, but later clarified that he had been joking about tapping the 57-year-old mixed martial arts tycoon for the job, though the two are set to meet. The post has remained vacant for several weeks.

Referring to his longtime friend as a “violent Fighter and Warrior,” Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social on Saturday that he had asked White to “bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country.”

“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” Trump claimed, listing Russian mixed martial artists Khabib Nurmagomedov and Islam Makhachev, current and former US fighters Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, and Kayla Harrison, as well as Brazil’s Amanda Nunes.

“Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other,” Trump stated.

Speaking to reporters after a boxing event in London on Saturday, White said he was heading to the US capital immediately. “I’m flying to Washington, DC right now,” he said.

Asked how he would balance the White House position with his existing responsibilities, White replied: “Yeah, I got a lot of jobs already.”

🚨 Dana White says he’s flying to Washington DC “right now” after President Trump offered him the White House press secretary role 👀 https://t.co/GGK3F2VUSr

— Championship Rounds (@ChampRDS) November 7, 2026

The UFC boss declined to elaborate on his previous conversations with Trump or say whether he intended to accept the offer. “We have a meeting on Monday, so I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that,” he said.

Earlier, White posted an AI-generated clip of himself at the podium in the White House press briefing room on Instagram, with the caption “On to the next chapter.”

🚨 JUST IN: Dana White drops this gem after President Trump offers him the job of White House press secretary “On to the next chapter” Make it happen, he’d have a blast with the fake news 😅🔥 Stephen Miller will likely keep slapping down the media himself in public as Chief of Staff! TIME TO UNLEASH

— Eric Daugherty (@EricLDaugh) November 7, 2026

Speaking to reporters in Florida on Sunday, Trump insisted that his offer had not been serious. “I was kidding, but I think Dana likes the idea, and he is a very capable guy,” he said, describing the announcement as “just a little fun.” Trump added that he would meet White at the White House on Monday to discuss other matters.

CNN had earlier reported, citing a source familiar with the matter, that White had declined the offer, while a White House aide confirmed that Trump was indeed joking about the offer.

Former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia stepped down in mid-October after just five days on the job, the shortest tenure of any White House press secretary in US history. The conservative political commentator had faced widespread criticism over her handling of her debut press briefing, as well as allegations that she had misrepresented herself as a lawyer after she failed to confirm whether she had passed a US bar exam.

Read more

She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who assumed the position after Trump returned to office in January 2025 and stepped down in August, ostensibly to spend more time with her family.

As for White, Trump has had a close relationship with the UFC CEO for years. The promotion company helped organize a fight on the White House South Lawn in June as part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of the US Declaration of Independence.

Speaking last April, White said that unlike multiple other sports organizations that barred Russian athletes from competitions after the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in 2022, the UFC had never ceased cooperation with mixed martial artists from the country.

The potential appointment comes amid a broader White House reshuffle following the Republicans’ bruising defeat in the midterm elections. On Friday, Trump announced that his longtime adviser, immigration hardliner Stephen Miller, would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, effective Monday. Wiles, who had served in the role since Trump returned to office, will move to his political operation.

title: Germany can’t spare more Patriots for Ukraine – defense minister
content:
Further donations of the US-made air defense systems would create critical shortages in Berlin’s own stocks, Boris Pistorius has said

Germany can’t provide Ukraine with any more US-made Patriot air defense systems because it would dangerously deplete its own stocks, Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has said.

In an interview with the newspaper Berliner Morgenpost published on Friday, Pistorius noted that Berlin had already delivered several Patriot systems and large numbers of guided missiles to Kiev.

“We cannot provide any more at this moment,” the German defense chief stated, explaining that anything Germany supplied now would not be replaced “for the foreseeable future.”

Pistorius urged other Western nations, whom he accused of having “contributed significantly less,” to step up deliveries of air defense systems to Ukraine.

Pistorius had already warned in January that Germany could not send any more Patriot systems, saying it had already handed over more than a third of its capabilities to Ukraine.

Germany, one of Kiev’s key Western backers, has launched a massive rearmament drive since the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in 2022, with Chancellor Friedrich Merz setting the goal of building Europe’s strongest conventional army. Berlin has cited a perceived threat from Russia, while Moscow has repeatedly dismissed as “nonsense” claims that it intends to attack NATO.

Apart from a shortage of Patriot air defense systems themselves, Ukraine has experienced significant shortages of modern PAC-3 missiles capable of intercepting ballistic rockets. The deficit intensified after Russia stepped up its long-range missile and drone strikes on military-related targets across Ukraine. Moscow has described its strikes as retaliation for Kiev’s UAV attacks on energy facilities and other civilian infrastructure inside Russia.

Intercepting ballistic missiles can require launching two Patriot interceptors at a single target, with each missile costing between $3.5 and $5 million. Russia, meanwhile, has repeatedly launched large-scale strikes involving dozens of missiles and hundreds of drones.

Read more

The US and its allies are also reportedly facing severe shortages of Patriot interceptors after Washington expended large quantities of air defense ammunition during its war against Iran earlier this year. The shortages have reportedly forced Washington to delay contracted deliveries of PAC-3 interceptors to some customers in Europe and Asia.

Nevertheless, Ukrainian leader Vladimir Zelensky has repeatedly demanded that Western backers provide Kiev with more interceptors.

Late last month, Ukrainian Defense Minister Evgeny Khmara asked France, Germany, Italy, the UK, and Poland to donate 10% of their respective interceptor stockpiles to Kiev.

However, the Netherlands and Poland had previously indicated that they had no Patriot missiles to spare, while other European countries are reportedly holding back their own PAC-3 reserves as well.

Moscow has consistently denounced Western weapons deliveries to Ukraine, arguing that they only serve to unnecessarily prolong the bloodshed without changing the conflict’s ultimate outcome, while increasing the risk of
a direct clash between Russia and NATO.

title: Iran won’t surrender. Can Russia give Trump another way out?
content:
Tehran’s outreach to Moscow opens space for a deal that could protect Iranian interests and give Washington a political win.

On November 5, Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of Iran Mohsen Rezaei in the Kremlin during the official’s working visit to Moscow. According to the Kremlin, the two sides discussed the development of bilateral cooperation under the Treaty on Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, as well as international and regional issues, with a particular focus on the situation in the Persian Gulf and the Middle East. The Kremlin also confirmed that Rezaei conveyed a message from the Supreme Leader of Iran Mojtaba Khamenei.

The fact that the meeting was also attended by Presidential Aide Yuri Ushakov and Head of the Main Directorate of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces Igor Kostyukov is quite notable. While the details of the conversation have not been disclosed, Kostyukov’s presence suggests that the discussions likely extended beyond political relations to include urgent security matters, which are of paramount concern for Iran.

Rezaei is an influential figure in Iran’s military and political landscape. As the former commander-in-chief of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), he has a strong reputation in military circles; he also has longstanding ties to influential clerics. Rezaei’s appointment as Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council and the task entrusted to him – that of personally delivering Khamenei’s message to Vladimir Putin – indicate the high level of trust placed in him by the Supreme Leader of Iran. Therefore, his trip to Moscow carries substantial weight. Rezaei advocates for a robust strategic alignment between Iran, Russia, and China, viewing these relationships as crucial for Iran’s security and independent foreign policy. His visit reaffirms that the strengthening of ties with Moscow is supported at the highest level in Tehran.

Read more

Another important aspect is the speed with which Rezaei arrived in Moscow. A phone call between Putin and Rezaei occurred on November 2, and just three days later, it was followed by the in-person meeting, in the course of which the message from the Supreme Leader was delivered. This signals that the matter could not be resolved remotely or through standard diplomatic channels. Such urgency is understandable. After eight months of war, both the US and Iran are exploring potential diplomatic breakthroughs while also bracing for renewed hostilities. American forces in the region are poised for a brief, intense campaign should US President Donald Trump authorize it. Trump himself has stated that he currently has no plans for new strikes but remains ready to act if necessary. However, Tehran understands that such assurances do not preclude future attacks. Consequently, the Iranian leadership cannot trust Washington’s public statements, but must take into account the likelihood of further escalation and determine what kind of support the country can count on. 

This uncertainty is exacerbated by discussions surrounding the potential use of weapons of mass destruction. Tucker Carlson has recently claimed that Trump is considering a nuclear strike on a site near Natanz, one of Iran’s key nuclear facilities. Trump responded that there is no need for such an attack; no further confirmation of Carlson’s claims has emerged. While American officials cited by major Western outlets assure that Washington has no intention of using nuclear weapons, such reassurances are insufficient for Tehran.

At the same time, a debate about chemical weapons is unfolding. According to recent reports, Israel has informed the US that Iran is allegedly contemplating the use of chemical weapons. Some American officials view these reports as an attempt to pressure Washington into resuming large-scale military operations. Meanwhile, the Gulf countries have reacted to the news with skepticism. Iran itself categorically denies possessing any chemical weapons. Even if the likelihood of extreme scenarios is low, such discussions force the Iranian leadership to consider worst-case scenarios and seek external support.

Read more

Mohsen Rezaei’s visit to Moscow takes on special significance amid evolving US-Russia relations. Trump explained his decision not to impose new sanctions on Russia by the desire not to disrupt negotiations over Ukraine. Washington is interested in maintaining dialogue with Moscow, and Russia is also open to dialogue. However, Russia has no intention of sacrificing its relationship with Tehran. Russia’s public reception of the Iranian envoy sends a clear message to those who hope that the warming ties between Russia and the US might come at Iran’s expense or that Russia may abandon its interests to please the White House. The message is clear: Moscow will choose its partners independently, and its relationship with Tehran holds intrinsic value. For the Iranian leadership, this meeting represents an opportunity to reaffirm mutual interest in collaboration and discuss how to advance it in the current circumstances.

There’s also a pragmatic aspect. As Russia’s role in the Iran issue becomes more prominent, there are more reasons for Moscow to be involved in the resolution of the conflict. On October 21, President Putin expressed Russia’s readiness to assist in addressing the crisis surrounding Iran. High-level contacts with Tehran lend weight to this statement ahead of possible negotiations: discussions are underway regarding a meeting between leaders, including Putin and Trump, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, which will be held on November 18-19.

Russia has the means to facilitate a resolution, and the absence of mutual defense obligations with Iran doesn’t negate that capacity. Moscow maintains ties with Tehran while also engaging with Washington. This position enables Russia to act as a mediator and allows it to offer a platform for talks, which Iran is keen to pursue, as achieving lasting peace is crucial for avoiding further military action. 

Read more

Following the Republicans’ defeat in the midterm elections, Trump has even more reasons to seek a diplomatic solution. The war in Iran has contributed to voter dissatisfaction, and its continuation may lead to heavier domestic political losses. However, there is also a chance that the US president may resort to military action to demonstrate resolve and prove that he can achieve his goals despite any opposition. Even so, another bombing campaign won’t secure victory for Trump. If Tehran withstands the pressure again and refuses to accept US terms, Trump will have to explain why the use of force didn’t yield the promised results. The political fallout would hit both him and the Republican Party hard. In this context, Russian mediation could also prove beneficial for Washington. Moscow may help the two sides form agreements that allow Iran to safeguard its interests while giving Trump a diplomatic win to present to the American public. This would require both sides to be open to compromise, but there is still room for diplomacy.

Additional opportunities emerge as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu loses his political standing. Netanyahu has been the main driver of the strategy of military pressure on Iran and the involvement of the US in the conflict. Following the elections, however, he faces a real threat of losing his position: Gadi Eisenkot holds an edge in the race to form a new government. While a shift in power isn’t guaranteed just yet, Netanyahu’s situation has certainly become more precarious. His departure wouldn’t resolve the underlying tensions between Israel and Iran, but it might alleviate some of the pressure on Washington. 

Against this backdrop, Rezaei’s visit to Moscow takes on significant meaning. It signals Tehran’s reliance on Russia as its primary political partner and a potential ally that may help resolve the crisis. For Moscow, this represents an opportunity to strengthen its ties with Iran and advocate for solutions that align with its own security interests in the region.

title: Irish ‘fake news’ expert exposed as fake – media
content:
An academic who taught aspiring journalists about fake news and disinformation has been accused of falsely claiming to hold a PhD

An Irish academic who built a career studying fake news and disinformation has been caught up in a misinformation scandal over a doctorate he apparently never earned, according to an investigation by national broadcaster RTE.

Tom Felle, an associate professor and former head of journalism at the University of Galway, one of Ireland’s leading universities, was referred to as ‘Dr Tom Felle’ for years. His supposed credentials appeared on university websites, recruitment materials, and social media. In his CV and an interview with RTE last summer, Felle claimed that he earned a journalism PhD in 2022 from London’s City University, now City St George’s, where he previously worked as a senior lecturer. Its journalism department ranks among Britain’s most prestigious.

However, an RTE Prime Time investigation published on Friday found that Felle was never awarded the doctorate he claimed to hold. A former senior academic at City St George’s told the broadcaster that Felle enrolled in a PhD program but left without completing it. Felle claimed that he earned his degree through previously published research, a legitimate route involving a shorter thesis. Yet he reportedly could not recall its title or explain its absence from the university library. He also said he had no supervisor or external examiner and had never defended his thesis – all requirements for obtaining a doctorate at City St George’s.

Read more

The university initially refused to confirm whether Felle was an alumnus, citing data protection. But a Freedom of Information request and subsequent review revealed that none of the four journalism PhDs awarded in 2021-22 and 2022-23 were earned through his supposed route.

Read more

The irony practically writes itself. Felle’s now-inaccessible University of Galway profile listed research interests including “trust” and “transparency,” along with “information disorder, verification, and the manipulation of online information.” His credentials helped establish him as a respected media expert: He won a US government-funded Fulbright scholarship in 2023, advised international organizations, and was listed among this year’s Irish Journalism Awards judges.
He has also published extensively on journalism, ethics, and disinformation. In a 2025 article on the BBC’s credibility crisis, he championed rigorous fact-checking and separating verified evidence from unsupported claims. In a 2017 Limerick Leader column criticizing accountability failures at the university, he declared: “Truth is uncomfortable but we all benefit from full transparency and accountability.”

The University of Galway declined to say whether it checked Felle’s qualifications prior to hiring him. Several university webpages have since been edited or deleted to remove his doctoral title. Felle did not respond to RTE’s requests for comment.

READ MORE: A generation of complete idiots? How AI is changing our children

Felle is hardly alone in academia’s growing hall of shame over dubious credentials. Just last month, Nigerian commentator Anthony Kila, a vocal champion of honesty and transparency, was accused of fabricating degrees and academic titles. Cambridge University in Britain faced its own embarrassment over sociologist Jason Arday, who resigned in August following disputed plagiarism allegations and questions about his credentials. Arday, who denied plagiarism, died days later. Cambridge subsequently ordered a review of its hiring practices.

title: Gunman opens fire in Polish city of Krakow, killing at least 6 people and injuring over a dozen
content:
Six people were killed and 15 wounded after a gunman opened fire Saturday afternoon in a busy market square in Krakow, Poland, authorities said.

The gunman, a 24-year-old Polish citizen, aimed at random people as he drove into the Main Square, a major tourist destination in the center of the city, Krakow police said. Four women and two men were killed. Two police officers were wounded, one seriously, Poland's interior minister said on X.

The perpetrator was shot and wounded during a gunfight with officers a short distance away from the initial violence, police said, and was taken to the hospital for surgery. The death toll earlier stood at five, but police updated it to six in a post on X.

Bomb threats hit more than a dozen European flights, forcing diversions and emergency landings

Katarzyna Ciso, a spokesperson for the Krakow police, said the perpetrator was wearing military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest and used a military-type long gun in the attack. Police found many other weapons, as well as ammunition, in his car. He kept firing at the police even after being shot himself, she said.

Ciso added that the gunman acted alone and that the public is safe.

It was not immediately clear whether the firearm used in Saturday's attack, or the guns found in the perpetrator's car, were legal. Around 411,000 people hold gun permits in Poland, which has a population of 37 million, and interest in gun ownership has been rising.

Mass shootings are uncommon in Poland. However, in mid-October three attacks at schools in the central province of Mazovia took place within four days, leaving one person dead and many wounded, including children.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, in a post on X, praised the police officers who responded to Saturday's tragedy. Polish President Karol Nawrocki said his thoughts were with the victims, the wounded and their families.

More than 600,000 rally across France to demand higher wages and school funding

"America stands with Poland at this dark hour as Poland stands with her beloved citizens of Krakow," Tom Rose, the U.S. ambassador to Poland, wrote on X.

Images from the scene showed police officers and ambulances covering the area, and a Polish Medical Air Rescue helicopter also landed in the square.

A tram driver reported around 3 p.m. that his vehicle was shot at from a man in a moving car while passing nearby the main square, the Krakow municipal transport company said. The window to the tram driver's cabin was shattered.

Around 15 million tourists a year visit Krakow, Poland's second-largest city, the majority passing through the Main Square.
